comparisons.peer_topic: FPGA and Adaptive SoC Platform Offerings
comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers FPGAs with reconfigurable hardware and integrated cores, and Adaptive SoCs targeting embedded systems with heterogeneous processing systems for real-time control and acceleration. Specific products include Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoCs for RF applications and the Versal portfolio for heterogeneous acceleration in big data and AI.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD provide customizable silicon platforms for customers targeting high-performance computing and AI workloads, but they differ in underlying technology and flexibility. AVGO provides IP platforms and technology for customers to design custom ASICs, which are built to specific customer specifications (e.g., integrating embedded logic, memory, and SerDes). In contrast, AMD offers FPGAs and Adaptive SoCs, which feature reconfigurable hardware, allowing for post-manufacturing flexibility rather than the fixed, custom nature of ASICs described by AVGO. AVGO focuses on the creation of bespoke silicon for AI/HPC, while AMD focuses on adaptable, reconfigurable platforms for acceleration and embedded systems.

sentences.text: • Custom Silicon Solutions: We provide advanced technology and intellectual property ("IP") platforms for customers to design and develop application specific integrated circuits ("ASICs") targeting AI and high-performance computing, networking and storage applications. Our custom silicon provides the platform to integrate embedded logic, memory, serializer/deserializer ("SerDes") technology, IP cores and processor cores. ASICs are custom products built to individual customers specifications.
We offer two types of platforms that support our customers' designs and reduce their development efforts: FPGAs and Adaptive SoCs.

FPGAs feature reconfigurable hardware as well as integrated memory, DSP, analog mixed signal, high-speed serial transceivers, and networking cores coupled with advanced software for a broad range of applications in all of our end markets.
This product portfolio is ideally suited to accelerate a broad set of applications in the emerging era of big data and AI.

peer_results.rationale: The provided candidates for INTC describe edge computing processor suites (Intel Core Ultra 200S) and specific process node manufacturing status (Intel 3). These disclosures focus on general-purpose desktop/data center processor launches and fabrication node transitions, rather than custom silicon/ASIC solutions, FPGA/Adaptive platforms, or specific AI/HPC storage acceleration solutions comparable to AVGO's custom silicon offerings. No candidate directly addresses the topic of providing custom or adaptable silicon platforms for AI/HPC in a way substantively comparable to AVGO's ASIC focus.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center AI and High-Performance Storage Offerings
comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for AI and big data is driving the need for high-performance storage; SBU addresses this with the 6500 30TB SSD for AI data lakes and sampled the 9550 series in 2024 for AI and high-performance computing workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU identify AI and high-performance computing as primary drivers for their respective product solutions, though the products themselves address different layers of the infrastructure stack. AVGO provides custom silicon (ASICs) with integrated processor cores and IP to handle the compute and networking aspects of AI and HPC. MU addresses the storage layer of these same workloads, noting that machine learning servers require fast data access and low latency, leading to demand for high-performance SSDs like the 9550 series sampled in 2024. AVGO's solution focuses on processing and interconnect technology, while MU's solution focuses on data storage performance for AI data lakes and HPC.

comparisons.peer_topic: Hardware Foundation: GPUs, DPUs, and CPUs
comparisons.peer_summary: The platform is founded on GPUs for parallel workloads, expanded in fiscal year 2022 to include DPUs and in fiscal year 2024 to include CPUs, allowing optimization across the computing, networking, and storage stack.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA explicitly position their platforms as enabling solutions for AI and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads, representing different architectural approaches to the same market need. AVGO provides custom silicon solutions (ASICs) that integrate processor cores, memory, and IP for customers to design bespoke accelerators. NVDA provides a foundational accelerated computing platform centered on GPUs, which excel at parallel workloads like neural network training and inferencing, and has expanded to include CPUs and DPUs. While NVDA offers a standardized, parallel-processing GPU-based platform, AVGO focuses on custom-integrated silicon solutions for specific customer requirements within the same AI/HPC domain.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and QCOM leverage heterogeneous computing architectures to enable high-performance processing, but they target different end-market applications. AVGO provides custom silicon platforms that integrate embedded logic, memory, and processors primarily for data center applications like AI, HPC, and networking. QCOM utilizes System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features (CPUs, GPUs, NPUs) to enable high-performance, low-power computing, primarily for mobile devices, connectivity, and increasingly automotive AI (on-device inference). While both use heterogeneity to boost performance, AVGO's focus is on data center infrastructure and custom AI accelerators, whereas QCOM's focus is on integrated, low-power edge and consumer computing.

Our custom silicon provides the platform to integrate embedded logic, memory, serializer/deserializer ("SerDes") technology, IP cores and processor cores. We have developed System-on-Chip (SoC) architecture with heterogeneous computing features, which uses our central processing unit (CPU) and different types of specialized engines (graphics processing unit (GPU) and neural processing unit (NPU)) to enable high-performance and low-power computing and other optimization techniques.
